title: Diwali Credit Card Shopping: Five Ways to Keep Festive Spending Under Control
excerpt: Budget before the sales, keep utilisation below 30-40% of your limit, take offers only on planned purchases, treat EMIs as commitments, and pay in full — the festive-season guidance in five steps.
body:
• Set a festive budget and a shopping list before Diwali and Dhanteras sales start, and treat your credit limit as a ceiling to stay well under — not as spending capacity.
  • Keep credit utilisation below 30-40% of your limit, CRIF High Mark advises, because higher utilisation can hurt your credit score.
  • Use festive offers only on planned purchases, be cautious with no-cost EMIs — the amount is blocked against your limit — and pay the full balance on time, not just the minimum due.
  • Track spending in real time through card apps or SMS alerts, and give unplanned purchases a 24-hour cooling period.

The festive trap: easy credit, hard statement

Diwali and Dhanteras bring the year's biggest sales, and credit cards make it easy to buy now and think later. Guidance published for the festive season — including a Livemint list on keeping Diwali and Dhanteras credit-card expenses under control, CRIF High Mark's Diwali credit guide and Paisabazaar's festive budgeting advice — converges on the same point: the card is a borrowing facility, not extra income, and every purchase has to be repaid when the statement arrives.

1. Budget first, list second

Both guides start before any shopping happens. Decide how much you can comfortably spend based on income, savings and existing commitments, divide it across categories such as clothes, gifts, electronics and decor, and make a list of what you actually need. A list keeps purchases focused and prioritised; a budget set in advance prevents the common festive pattern where digital payments make spending feel invisible until the statement lands.

2. Watch your utilisation, not just your balance

CRIF High Mark notes that using more than 30-40% of your credit limit raises your credit utilisation ratio, a factor that affects your credit score, and that exceeding the limit can trigger penalties. If you hold more than one card, spreading purchases across cards keeps utilisation lower on each. Paisabazaar adds a timing tactic: spread festive expenses between two statement cycles so one month's bill does not absorb the whole season.

3. Take offers only on planned buys

Cashback, bonus points and instant discounts are useful only when they apply to something already on your list. CRIF advises checking hidden terms such as processing fees, minimum spends and capped cashback, and avoiding signing up for multiple new cards just for short-term deals. Paisabazaar makes the same point about reward points: do not shop just to earn them, because only a small fraction of the amount spent returns as points.

4. Treat EMIs as commitments, not discounts

No-cost EMIs can spread a big purchase over up to 9 months on selected items and cards, Paisabazaar notes, but the full purchase amount is blocked against your credit limit, which can push utilisation up and affect your score. CRIF similarly warns that even no-cost EMIs may carry processing charges, that stacking EMIs raises monthly obligations, and that missing an EMI affects your credit report. Use them sparingly, for items with long-term value.

5. Pay in full, on time, and track as you go

Paying only the minimum due avoids a late fee for that cycle but leaves interest accumulating on the unpaid balance. Both guides advise paying the outstanding amount in full by the due date, setting reminders or auto-pay, and monitoring transactions in real time through card apps or SMS alerts so you can adjust before you overshoot. For impulse buys triggered by flash sales and countdown timers, CRIF suggests a 24-hour cooling period — the urge often fades, and the money stays in your account.
